reference.title: Exercise Ball Body Saw
reference.listing: Catalog entry only (gymvisual.com not read; blocked by the proxy). Movement from the exercise name and standard coaching.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you saw back, in as you come forward; keep the brace.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s back, 0.5 s hold, 1.5 s forward

cues.text: Forearms on the mat under the shoulders, shins on the ball, body in one straight line.
Breathe out and push the body back, shoulders sliding behind the elbows.
Hold the line; no sag at the hips.
Breathe in and pull the body forward until the shoulders are over the elbows.

mistakes.mistake: Hips sagging as you go back
mistakes.fix: Shorten the saw; brace the abs and squeeze the glutes.
Keep shoulders, hips and ankles in one line.
Push the floor away through the forearms.
Smooth, controlled saw; the ball should roll, not bounce.

kinematics.norm: Shoulders slide about 10-15 cm behind the elbows (clinical opinion)
Planted under the shoulders at the start (standard forearm plank)

kinematics.setup: 55 cm ball under the shins (gap 0.3 to 0.8 cm)
kinematics.norm: Prone work on a Swiss ball raises abdominal demand (Escamilla 2016; Oliva-Lozano 2020)

kinematics.peak: 1.4 s back, 0.5 s hold, 1.6 s forward

sources.title: GymVisual #14471, Exercise Ball Body Saw, video (movement reference)
Escamilla, Lewis, Pecson, Imamura and Andrews 2016, muscle activation among supine, prone and side position exercises with and without a Swiss ball (Sports Health 8(4):372-379; PMC4922527)
Oliva-Lozano and Muyor 2020, core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Use a ball rated for exercise, inflated firm, on a non-slip mat.
Low-back pain: stop; regress to a front plank.
modify: Ball further up the legs (thighs) for a shorter lever.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis resists the trunk sagging as the lever lengthens (Escamilla 2016; Oliva-Lozano 2020).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Brace the trunk on the unstable ball (Escamilla 2016).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Brace the trunk on the unstable ball (Escamilla 2016).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull the body forward again (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull the body forward again (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Hold the shoulder blades as the arms reach overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Hold the shoulder blades as the arms reach overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Keeps the hips in line (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Keeps the hips in line (clinical opinion).
